newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end mostly higher.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended mostly higher, as the market continued to consolidate in ranges despite a slightly disappointing two-year note auction, traders and analysts said.
"The auction was somewhat disappointing," David Ader, managing analyst at Technical Data, said. "Given how much interest it generated, it just didn't deliver."

Ader said the cumulative volume was 150 percent of normal, yet the Treasury department's auction of $18.75 billion two-year notes produced an average estimate of 6.17 percent. Traders were looking for a yield of 6.16 percent.
Ader also said the bid-to-cover ratio was weaker than expected at 2.23.
However, September T-bonds closed pit trade above their 100-day moving average at 108-23/32. On Monday, the contract closed below its 100-day moving average for the first time all month.

Ader noted anticipation ahead of overnight trade, as 12 out of the last 15 trading have started with a slight bid due to gains in Tokyo and European markets. Despite one large institution selling 1,000 September contracts at the opening, speculators were covering short positions, traders said.
Traders said good buying in the cash two- to five-year note sector overnight spilled in the opening of trade.

One hedge fund was reportedly buying two-year cash notes, while one Middle Eastern central bank bought $750 million in cash two-year notes and another Saudi Arabian account purchased $300 million in 10-year notes.

One U.S. bank steadily sold 4,000 September bonds all day, and sold 3,000 March Eurodollars. Earlier this bank was a heavy seller of the two-year Eurodollar strip. There was little activity in note futures, despite several good buyers of five- and 10-year notes.

However, the bond and Eurodollar markets held their firm tone throughout the day. The August U.S. consumer confidence number, which rose to 109.4, versus estimates of 104.4, briefly rattled the market.
September bonds fell to 108-22/32, but found little selling pressure, they said.
The 0.9-percent rise in the weekly Redbook Retail Sales Index had little affect on the market. Traders, on average, were expecting a weaker number.

At the end of pit trade, September bonds were 10/32 higher at 108-30/32, 10-year notes were up 05/32 at 107-09/32, munibonds 24/32 higher at 114-17/32, December Eurodollars were up one basis point at 94.08, March Eurodollars were also up one bps at 93.91, and March T-bills were up one bps at 94.50.
